cells.tense: You are here, and what the heart knows is steady enough to use.
cells.ask: Pick the one account you keep that runs against you, and settle it today — yours to yours.
cells.core:
You sit with what you know before you act, and the sitting is doing work, not stalling. What you know is quiet and doesn't need to win an argument — you weigh what's in front of you and the balance comes back on its own. People feel that evenness and stand a little steadier next to it.

This is one part of your life, not all of it, and in this part the ear is still open. The calm is worth keeping, and keeping it costs something: something gets put down. Find the account still running against you — the favor you didn't call in, the apology you're owed, the debt you stopped counting — and close it today, on your own terms. Then see what that frees.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a settlement that hasn't arrived and may not need to.
cells.ask: Name the outcome you're waiting for, and pick one part of it you'll stop tracking today.
cells.core:
You're already living past the ending. The fairness hasn't landed yet, so you rehearse it — what you'll say, what they'll finally understand, where the scales will tip. Each talk becomes a chance to bring it forward. The bracing is tiring and it hasn't moved the day closer.

What's been lost is the ability to let something be finished without a verdict. So declare one piece of it closed, even if the rest stays open. Say what you're waiting for out loud, pick the part you'll stop tracking, and let the waiting happen without you holding the pen. What you've already gathered from all this is yours whether or not the score is ever settled.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Write down the three thoughts you keep circling, one sentence each, then read them to someone you trust.
cells.core:
When this part of you is working, you hear what's off and you say so — a small correction, made early, before the gap widens. You do it without heat. You notice what someone carried and you name it in front of them, and the two of you even it out between you. It's ordinary and it keeps things clean.

Lately the weighing happens at a distance, if it happens. You talk about it like it belongs to someone else. What steadies you here isn't more feeling — don't force that. It's getting the scattered pieces into one line you can hold. Write down the three thoughts you keep circling, one sentence each. Then read them to someone who'll take them seriously. Whatever comes back does the evening out you can't do alone right now.

cells.tense: You are already evening things out, and you call it just how you are.
cells.ask: Tell one person about a time you quietly made something right, without calling it anything.
cells.core:
You're already the one adjusting the proportions. You notice what's out of balance and nudge it — a word here, a piece of the check there, a silence you let stand so someone else can speak. It works, and you'd say it's nothing, just being decent.

But the adjusting costs you, and nobody's covering it, least of all you. So take one of those moments and name it to a person you trust — not as a virtue, just as a fact of how you spend yourself. Say what you did and what it cost. That's how the depths stay open, and how you stop being the only one who doesn't know what you're carrying.
